theorem.statement_text:
IsCompact projectorSet ∧
    projectorSet ⊆ traceOneSymmetric ∧
    Metric.diam projectorSet = Real.sqrt 2 ∧
    ¬ HasTenSmallCover

insight.obstacle: A geometric non-covering claim is not directly in the form required by the finite combinatorial obstruction theorem.
insight.strategy: Translate a hypothetical cover into the explicitly modeled Admissible representation; derive a finite support-face incidence system; show that it satisfies the hypotheses of a forbidden finite-configuration theorem; conclude by contradiction. Keep the geometric-to-combinatorial bridge as a separately audited lemma rather than treating the combinatorial contradiction as self-justifying.
preconditions: A cover-to-representation map is defined and preserves the exact cover count and diameter constraints.
The translated representation satisfies every hypothesis of the finite obstruction theorem, including the support-face incidence conditions.
The target problem admits a finite combinatorial encoding with the same relevant forbidden-configuration structure.
Cardinality and dimension-specific assumptions are checked afresh; the current theorem is a specific ten-set / rank-one-projector construction.

transformation.before_state: A hypothetical cover of the geometric projector set has not yet been converted into an object accepted by the finite obstruction theorem.
transformation.after_state: Use cover_to_admissible to construct Admissible data; Admissible.support_ten_system derives FiniteObstruction.TenSystem; FiniteObstruction.no_ten_system rules out the resulting object and hence the hypothesized cover.
transformation.expected_obligation_change: Split the proof into (1) faithful representation, (2) preservation of incidence/support constraints, and (3) a finite no-go theorem. A new domain needs new obligations for all three steps; similarity of prose is not enough.

evidence.supports: A candidate Admissible object induces a finite support-face system with the required combinatorial properties.
The support-system construction and the finite no-ten-system result contradict existence of an Admissible ten-configuration.
The main theorem uses the cover-to-Admissible bridge to discharge the non-covering conclusion.
The target property fixes a cover with ten sets, each contained in the projector set and with diameter strictly below √2.

failure_boundaries: If cover_to_admissible does not preserve coverage, membership, or the strict diameter bound, the final contradiction does not establish the intended geometric claim.
A finite obstruction result cannot be transferred to a different number of sets, dimension, incidence rule, or geometry without proving its hypotheses for that target.
The current finite case structure is tailored to the rank-one projectors in ℝ⁴ and ten sets; no extension to arbitrary dimensions is established.
The proof of the combinatorial obstruction may carry substantial domain-specific case analysis; the high-level strategy alone does not provide such a certificate.

transfer_candidates.rationale: Rejected as a direct mathematical transfer after inspecting the training-family target. Source family 156 refutes a ten-set small-diameter cover by mapping a hypothetical cover to Admissible data, deriving a finite support-face system, then invoking a finite no-ten-system theorem. Target family 157's OAI.HadwigerCounterexample.not_hadwiger_conjecture is established through an analytic/exponential graph construction, a small connected-matching bound, a matching-minor inequality, and a chromatic-number lower bound. Both are contradiction-based graph/geometry arguments at a very broad level, but the source's actual finite support-face transformation has no demonstrated structural role in the target proof. This is a curator's static negative-control annotation, not a measured failed model attempt and not an empirical transfer score.

directional_contract.source_move_requires: A hypothetical small-diameter cover of rank-one orthogonal projectors must be transformed into Admissible data and then a finite support-face incidence system satisfying the ten-system obstruction hypotheses.
directional_contract.target_goal_requires: Construct arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two and small connected-matching number, then apply a matching–minor inequality and a chromatic lower bound to obtain h(G) < chi(G).
notes: Both arguments end in contradiction, but the source representation map and finite support-face relation do not supply the graph witness or invariant inequalities required by the target.
Judgment is based on source-level static review; no generated transfer was attempted and this is not a measured trial.

source_obligation.quantifier_scope: The fixed rank-one-projector set in the nine-dimensional affine space cannot be covered by ten subsets of strictly smaller diameter.
preconditions: The target cover has exactly ten sets.
Each cover set lies inside the projector set and has diameter strictly below sqrt(2).
cover_to_admissible preserves coverage and the strict diameter constraints.

target_obligation.quantifier_scope: For every sufficiently large size bound, construct a finite graph whose chromatic number exceeds its clique-minor number.
preconditions: A graph-witness construction exists for arbitrarily large size bounds.
The connected-matching and independence-number invariant bounds hold for each witness.
The matching-minor inequality and chromatic lower bound apply to the same witness graph.
